title: Desktop
summary: The same app with a mouse and a keyboard, as a download for macOS, Windows and Linux.
description: The app was built for touch. On a desktop nothing may depend on a gesture or on the system's back button, and the window is used for more than one phone-sized column.

requirements.text: Every push to `main` publishes the desktop app on the `latest` release next to the APK: a disk image for Apple silicon Macs and one for Intel Macs, a Windows installer, and an AppImage and a `.deb` for Linux.
Without a Developer ID certificate the app is signed ad hoc, so it runs on Apple silicon after the user confirms it once. With one it is signed, and notarized when the Apple ID secrets are set.

The window first opens at 1280 by 860, and after that where and as large as it was closed. From 768 px wide the main sections are in a sidebar, and from 1200 px the sidebar shows their names next to the icons.
Everything that reacts to a press reacts to the pointer resting on it. Icon buttons show their name.
A screen that can be pulled down to refresh has a refresh button where there is a mouse, and refreshes on Cmd or Ctrl+R without reloading the web view.
Escape closes the dialog or menu on top, and only that one. Without one open it takes focus out of a field.

A dialog takes keyboard focus when it opens, keeps Tab inside it, and gives focus back when it closes. With a mouse its first text field is focused; on touch none is, so the keyboard doesn't cover it.
The arrow keys move through a menu and Enter picks an item.
Back and forward work from the keyboard (Cmd+[ and Cmd+], Alt+Left and Alt+Right) and from the mouse's back and forward buttons.
`/` and Cmd or Ctrl+K open search with its field focused. A single-key shortcut never fires while typing in a field.
Settings list the shortcuts where there is a mouse.

From 1100 px wide a diff shows the old file on the left and the new one on the right: unchanged lines on both sides, and in a run of removed and added lines the first removed next to the first added. Each side wraps, so neither scrolls sideways.
A line on either side can be selected for a comment, and a comment shows below the row its line is in.
Side by side is a preference, on by default, with a button next to the diff and a switch in Settings. Narrower windows always get one column.
One platform's build failing doesn't keep the others from publishing.

questions: Should the Windows installer be signed, so SmartScreen doesn't ask?
Should the desktop app update itself?
